question: The functions \(\sin(x)\) and \(\cos(x)\) are periodic with least period \(2\pi.\) What is the least period of the function \(\cos(\sin(x))?\)
solution:
Adding \(\pi\) to the input reverses the sign of sine, and cosine takes equal values at opposite inputs. Thus, for \(f(x)=\cos(\sin x)\),
\[
f(x+\pi)=\cos(-\sin x)=\cos(\sin x)=f(x).
\]
So \(\pi\) is a period.

To prove it is the least positive period, suppose \(T>0\) is any period. Then \(f(T)=f(0)=1\). The equation \(\cos u=1\) holds exactly when \(u=2k\pi\) for an integer \(k\). Since \(\sin T\) lies in \([-1,1]\), this forces \(\sin T=0\). Therefore \(T=n\pi\) for a positive integer \(n\), so \(T\geq\pi\).

The least period is \(\boxed{\pi}\), choice B.
